f7a77efce9d6b108f075d048f0885132df9d1ea5.summary: Analysis by Zyad Waleed Elzyat of the Auto-Color Linux backdoor, first documented by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 in February 2025. Without root, the sample runs in the background, keeps state in a temporary directory and repeatedly tries to reach a remote server. As root, it installs an embedded 35,160-byte library and registers it in the preload configuration file, creating a user-space rootkit that hides the implant's files and filters network socket listings. Earliest samples date from November to December 2024; observed targets were universities and government offices in North America and…

f7ece8e2fcdf3adeaa01c3c4ce3254dab3bbc13f.summary: Sygnia's forensic report describes a late-2023 intrusion at a large organization, which Sygnia links to a China-nexus state-sponsored actor it tracks as Velvet Ant. The actor kept access for about three years using PlugX malware, an internal file server as command-and-control, and two exposed F5 BIG-IP appliances. After eradication, the actor reappeared through dormant footholds. Four tools were found on the appliances. Sygnia says attribution is difficult and cannot rule out a false-flag operation.

f7fa3bcb72b159a9dc93724dd582f2df15436e02.summary: Blog post by Phil Stokes at SentinelOne, published 2019-12-05, continuing a macOS red-team proof of concept. It describes running native Apple API code through AppleScript/Objective-C without compiled binaries, spoofing an administrator authorization dialog to capture a user's password, and using a scheduled cron job for repeated execution. The author presents it as educational material for defenders and says threat actors are unlikely to use these techniques in the wild.
